items.applicant: a transparency activist, co-convenor of the National Campaign for People's Right to Information
items.asked: A copy of any independent appraisal or study on which the Commission decided to begin the SIR across the country in 2025, and the files, notings and records on that decision, with time to inspect them.
items.answer: The Times of India reported that the CPIO pointed to the guidelines of 24 June 2025 and said no further information was available, and The News Minute reported that on first appeal the Commission's Principal Secretary wrote that the Commission had not taken any decision on a nationwide SIR in 2025.
items.quote: Appellant is informed that the Commission has so far not taken any decision on initiating a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) across the country in 2025 and hence no information to be provided in this regard.
items.headline: Who decided on nationwide SIR? EC's RTI response raises questions
items.note: Two stages of one application. The CPIO reply of 27 August 2025 is reported by The Times of India (quote: 'You may refer to Commission's guidelines dated June 24, 2025 which is self- explanatory and available on the Commission's website.' and 'Further, no information in this regard is available in the Commission'). The first appellate reply signed by the Principal Secretary is undated in the reports and was posted by the applicant on X on 24 September 2026. The News Minute also reports that the CPIO had not provided the files 'as the requisite information is not available with him in any material form.'

items.applicant: a transparency activist, co-convenor of the National Campaign for People's Right to Information
items.asked: The order or notification for the 2003 intensive revision of Bihar's rolls and the guidelines for that revision, including the forms and documents required.
items.answer: Deccan Herald and The Times of India reported that the CPIO sent only the link to the 2025 SIR guidelines of 24 June 2025 and gave nothing on the 2003 revision.
items.quote: The EC did not provide the details sought under RTI and again provided the June 24 order.
items.headline: Election Commission refuses to provide 2003 Bihar SIR order on RTI query
items.note: The quote is the outlet's sentence. The reply did not say in words that no record is held, it supplied an unrelated document, so the outcome label is an approximation. Scroll reported on 10 July 2025, outside the RTI process, that a Commission official said the 2003 instruction could not be traced.

items.asked: All files, notings, correspondence, minutes, presentations and drafts on the SIR ordered on 24 June 2025, and a list of the files recording it.
items.answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Commission replied with a link to a page of 'comprehensive instructions' dated 14 July 2025 that the outlet could not open, and did not name any file on the decision.
items.quote: However, in response to our RTI application, the ECI provided a weblink to a back-end page on its website, which cannot be publicly accessed. These, ECI claimed, were “comprehensive instructions” dated July 14, 2025, which were self-explanatory, but we could not access them.
items.headline: A Dead Weblink: The Election Commission of India Demands Citizens' Records but Withholds Its Own Under RTI Law
items.note: The applicant reports the application was filed shortly after the 24 June 2025 announcement. It said it would appeal. No outcome of an appeal was found. Outcome label is approximate because the reply pointed to instructions the applicant could not open.

items.authority: Ministry of Law and Justice, transferred to the Election Commission of India
items.asked: Whether the Commission sought the Law Ministry's legal opinion on the SIR and, if so, the full paper trail of files, correspondence, memos, notes and presentations.
items.answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Ministry said it keeps no record of such advice and transferred the request to the Commission, which replied on 20 August 2025 that it had no information.
items.quote: On August 20, 2025, the ECI responded, stating it had no information available.
items.headline: A Dead Weblink: The Election Commission of India Demands Citizens' Records but Withholds Its Own Under RTI Law
items.note: The Ministry's reply is shown as an image in The Reporters' Collective's thread of late July 2025 (before the Supreme Court hearing of 28 July 2025). The outlet says it appealed the Ministry's reply. No appeal outcome was found.

items.authority: CEO Bihar, transferred to the 38 DEOs
items.asked: How many times EROs sent speed post notices to absent or shifted electors during the SIR, how many replies they received and how many notices came back undelivered.
items.answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the CEO sent the application to all 38 district election offices and that after eleven months only the Dulhin Bazar subdivision of Patna and the Hajipur district office had replied, the first saying it sent no speed post notices and the second saying electors were marked from the BLOs' door to door survey.
items.quote: The Dulhin Bazar subdivision of Patna has confirmed that it did not follow the written down existing processes to purge shifted voters. It had not contacted any of the absent or shifted voters via speed post.
items.headline: Did You Follow the Laid Down Rules During SIR? Not in Bihar, Say Election Officials
items.note: The quote is the outlet's characterisation of the Dulhin Bazar reply, whose image appears on the page. Filing date not stated, the article says eleven months had passed. 36 of 38 district offices had not replied by July 2026, which by the outlet's account is beyond the 30 day limit.

items.asked: File notings on the decision to begin the second phase of the SIR and the minutes of all meetings held on it.
items.answer: The Wire reported that after a first appeal the Commission supplied two pages of file notings showing the proposal initiated by an Under Secretary on 27 October 2025 and approved the same day, and supplied no minutes of meetings.
items.quote: The CPIO did not provide a response within the statutory time limit. In the first appeal, the CPIO attributed the delay to workload constraints. The RTI application, filed on November 29, 2025, was finally responded to on March 19, 2026 – more than three months after the prescribed period.
items.headline: If Voter Rolls Were Properly Maintained, Would SIR Be Needed? RTI Records Tell the Story.
items.note: The page shows an image of the notings. The same article covers the writer's other applications on Sections 22, 31 and 32 of the Representation of the People Act 1950 to the ECI, several CEOs, DEOs and EROs (Navsari, Choriyasi, seven Delhi EROs including Badarpur, which refused under Section 8(1)(j)). Those concern routine roll maintenance from 2018 to 2025 and are not counted here as SIR applications.

items.answer: Deccan Herald (PTI) reported that the Commission held the software questions exempt under Section 8(1)(d), said no module or separate procurement had been made for the West Bengal SIR, and directed the question on flagged electors to the EROs.

items.quote: These include appeals against inclusion and appeals against exclusion.

items.note: The quote is the reply's own footnote as The Wire reports it. The Wire shows images of the application and tables. items.asked: How many cases the Commission had referred to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955 after deletions in the SIR, as the Supreme Court directed in May 2026, for Bihar and for each state and union territory where the revision was complete, with a split by gender.
items.answer: The Commission's information officer replied after 50 days that it held none of the information. He said the counts might be with the Chief Electoral Officers of the states but did not transfer the application to them.
items.quote: After 50 days (against the statutory deadline of 30 days), its Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) replied (see Image 3 below) saying that it did not have any of the information sought in the RTI application.

items.note: Written by the applicant organisation's Director. The reply date is the filing date plus the 50 days the article gives; the reply itself is reproduced as an image and its date is not printed in the text. A companion application to the Ministry of Home Affairs is rti-13.

items.asked: The name and designation of the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955 for cases referred after deletions in the SIR in Bihar and the other states and union territories, and how many cases the Commission had referred to it.

The Commission replied after 40 days, passing the questions on the competent authority back to the Ministry of Home Affairs and the questions on the counts to the Chief Electoral Officer, Bihar. No answer naming the authority had been reported.

items.asked: Whether the Commission had compiled and shared with the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955 a list of people deleted in the SIR whom it held not to be citizens, as the Supreme Court directed, for the 13 states and union territories where the revision was complete, the number referred in each, and the number referred from Bihar and from West Bengal separately.
items.answer: The Commission's Central Public Information Officer answered none of the questions. By a letter of 29 July 2026 he transferred the whole application under section 6(3) to the information officer of the Chief Electoral Officer, Bihar, saying the information may be available there. The Reporters' Collective reported that it got no answer for the other twelve states.
items.quote: With reference to the application dated 01.07.2026 of ..., I am to state that the information sought may be available with your office. Accordingly, the application of ... is being transferred to your office under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 for replying directly to the applicant.

The quote is from the letter, with the applicant's name, a reporter of the Collective, left out. The questions in 'asked' are read from the query column of the replies (queries 3 and 4), which repeat the application. The article says the application was filed after the Supreme Court's four-week deadline, with 13 states and union territories done. Companion to rti-15. Related: rti-12 and rti-13 (CHRI asked the same question of the Commission and the Home Ministry in August).

items.authority: Electoral Registration Officers of Bihar's assembly constituencies, on transfer from the Chief Electoral Officer, Bihar
items.asked: Whether a list of people deleted in the SIR as not citizens had been compiled and referred to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955, and how many people from Bihar had been referred.
items.answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that more than 100 Electoral Registration Officers in Bihar replied. The two replies it reproduces, from Brahampur (199) and Buxar (200), answer 'No' to whether any list was compiled and referred, and answer the question on numbers referred with the constituency's SIR figures by reason (death, permanently shifted, duplicate, other). Neither has a category for people found not to be citizens.
items.quote: We received responses from assembly constituencies in the state; while they gave clear numbers of voters deleted as absent, shifted, dead, and others, missing from their disclosures was any mention of a non-Indian citizen found.
items.headline: Amit Shah and ECI claim SIR Was to Catch ‘Infiltrators’. Commission Has no Record of Them
items.note: Outcome is 'supplied' because the officers answered the question ('No'); a second reader may prefer 'no record held', which is how the article puts it ('assembly election officials held zero records of non-citizens found'). Reply dates are not printed in the text; the Brahampur reply carries a handwritten date that reads 10.9.26 and is not entered. The figures in the two replies match the site's Bihar phase 1 reasons (data/bihar/raw/reasons_by_ac.csv.gz): Buxar dead 6,161, duplicate 1,609, other 1,840 exactly and shifted 15,964 against 15,949; Brahampur dead 8,885, duplicate 1,597, other 1,834 exactly and shifted 12,208 against 12,207. The 'more than 100' replies are the outlet's count; only two are shown. Companion to rti-14.

items.authority: Election Commission of India (First Appellate Authority)

items.asked: Not stated in the order or in the applicant's post. The Central Public Information Officer had said the information sought was spread across multiple files running to hundreds of pages.
items.answer: In First Appeal No. 3741, the Principal Secretary, as First Appellate Authority, recorded the officer's view that compiling the information would disproportionately divert the Commission's resources under Section 7(9). He noted that the Commission's information officers carry substantial election duties as their primary work and must balance them with replies under the Act, and advised a fresh application in clear and limited points. The appeal was disposed of. The order does not say what was asked, so whether it concerned the revision is not known.
items.quote: In this regard, it may be noted that the CPIOs of the Election Commission of India are entrusted with substantial election-related responsibilities, which constitute their primary official duties.

His post says RTI requests are being rejected on the claim that 'Public Information Officers of ECI have other work and are busy'. The order cites Section 7(9), adds the duties sentence, and disposes of the appeal with advice to file afresh. The CPIO's own reply is referred to as an attachment and was not published.

items.applicant: a transparency activist and retired naval officer
items.asked: The application itself is not reported. The reply carried the Cabinet Secretariat's notes on the letters the two Election Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary on 29 July 2026.
items.answer: The notes show that both Commissioners complained that the Senior Deputy Election Commissioner had revised the work allocation among senior officers without consulting the Commission, and one of them added that the Administration Division had not given him the file when he asked for it. A note of 3 August proposed seeking the Chief Election Commissioner's opinion. A later note held that the letters were written in the Commissioners' individual capacities, that the Commission's business is to be decided unanimously where possible and by majority otherwise under Section 18 of the 2023 Act, and that acting without an official communication from the Commission as a whole may be inappropriate and could be construed as interference in the functioning of the Constitutional Body. The Cabinet Secretary signed that note and acknowledged both letters on 5 August, with a copy of the acknowledgement to the Chief Election Commissioner's office. The note was also marked to the Department of Personnel and Training and the Establishment Officer, to place the matter on record for future decisions about the officer. No other action was taken. The Commission had said on 26 September that the revised orders were never put into effect after the two Commissioners' directions.
items.quote: The above communications are from the ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the Commission as a whole.
items.headline: Instead of Taking Action on Concerns Raised by Two ECs, Cabinet Secretary Forwarded Their Letters to CEC's Office, RTI Reveals
items.note: The Wire Staff, posted 22 October 2026, 9:52 pm IST, read in full on 23 October 2026 from The Wire's content API with curl. The Wire prints images of two paragraphs of the Cabinet Secretary's note and of both letters, which were read directly. The quote is from the note as imaged. Business Today (23 October, 8:08 am IST, with PTI) was read in full for the dates of 3 and 5 August and the marking to DoPT. The applicant is named in the reports, and the site gives applicants by role. The documents concern the work allocation order. The reports tie it to the revision through The Indian Express account of oversight of the roll software, which is on the process page. Dates of filing and reply are not reported.

items.applicant: a social activist in Karimnagar, Telangana
items.asked: The name and version of the software, application or AI platform used to detect errors or inconsistencies in voter data during the revision, whether it flags records for verification, correction or deletion and what happens next, whether artificial intelligence, machine learning or automated decision tools were used at any stage, the safeguards against flagging genuine electors wrongly, and who reviews or approves a flagged record before action is taken.
items.answer: The Commission declined to give the name and version of the software under Section 8(1)(d), which covers commercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual property. It said no new software had been developed or procured for the revision. It called the questions on automatic flagging, artificial intelligence and safeguards a clarification, which it said falls outside the definition of information in Section 2(f). On who reviews flagged records it cited Section 8(1)(g), and added that under Sections 13B(1) and 13B(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 the Electoral Registration Officer of each constituency prepares and revises its roll and decides inclusion or exclusion on the basis of facts and records.
items.quote: no new software has been developed or procured for the SIR exercise
items.headline: Details of software used in SIR exempt from RTI, Election Commission cites 'trade secrets'
items.note: Refused. Himanshi Dahiya in the Hindustan Times, 25 October 2026, 6:35 am IST. The report gives the reply's date and not the application's. The applicant has posted the reply on RTI Library, which needs a sign-in to read. The Commission gave a similar answer on 21 July to a question about the West Bengal module, in the reply above that cites the same section.
